title: pravapis conformance case
description: One line of conformance/cases.jsonl. The file is JSON Lines: one object per line, UTF-8, LF endings, no trailing comma, no wrapping array. NORMATIVE: an implementation is conformant for a given data version iff it reproduces every case in the corpus generated from that version. Cases are generated from the data by `pravapis export-conformance` and are never written by hand. Version 2 adds the `offsets` kind and its `spans` field: the response contract (docs/API.md) includes code-point offsets into the output, and a port can produce the right text with the wrong offsets, so the corpus pins them directly.

id.description: Stable identifier. Stable across regenerations as long as the underlying case stays put, so a port can track a specific failure over time.

kind.description: At which level the case applies — the project's test material is not all of one kind, and running a unit case through the whole pipeline would fail for the wrong reason.

oneOf.title: Apply the single rule named in `rule`, alone, to `in` (already lowercased), with etymology resolved from the stem inventory if that rule is class-gated. Expect `out`. This is NOT the converter's output for that word: palat.assim turns свіння into сьвіння, while the pipeline goes on to write сьвіньня.
Apply the scheme named in `script` directly to `in`, with no orthography conversion (the --no-convert path). Expect `out`.

A bug that was fixed and must stay fixed. Convert `in` through the public API in `direction` and expect `out`. Pinned in both directions, because the bug was that one direction invented something the other could not undo. A case whose `in` and `out` are identical is one where the converter used to change a word it should have left alone — the kind a port is most likely to reintroduce, since a rule that overreaches looks correct in isolation.
Convert the whole of `in` through the public API in `direction`. Expect `out` exactly. From the trusted hand-written gold subset.
The same as `gold`, on genuine Taraškievica that nobody derived from a Narkamaŭka source.

Convert `in` through the public API in `direction`, expect `out`, AND expect `spans` to be the (start, end, from, to) of each change. `start`/`end` are Unicode CODE POINT indices into `out`. This is the kind that catches a port indexing strings in UTF-16 code units: it produces `out` correctly and `spans` wrong, and every other kind of case passes.

direction.description: The orthography conversion to perform. Null for `translit` cases, which change script and not spelling.

script.description: `cyrillic` for orthography cases; for a `translit` case, the name of the scheme to apply, as declared in its table's `scheme` field.

rule.description: Present on `rule` cases only: which rule to apply in isolation.

spans.description: Present only on `offsets` cases. One entry per change, in document order: [start, end, from, to]. `start` and `end` are Unicode code point indices into `out` — NOT UTF-16 code units, NOT byte offsets, NOT indices into `in`.

allOf.title: A rule case must name its rule
A translit case has no orthography direction
